answer: The walnut cap is applied at intake and tide exposes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a fleet in one epoch however much capital it holds, since every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 3 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a signal tag. That is 8 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
